# package sec

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/sec"
```

Package sec is the application-layer security of IEC 60870-5-104: the A-Profile of IEC 62351-5:2023 as IEC TS 60870-5-7:2025 maps it onto IEC 60870-5-101 and -104.

Two stations first agree on update keys (the Station Association: their certificates are exchanged, checked against what each side trusts, and an ECDH key agreement followed by HKDF gives both the same keys), then on session keys (the Session Key Change: the controlling station wraps fresh keys with the update keys). From then on every application ASDU travels inside a Secure Data message (S\_SD\_NA\_1) that is authenticated with a truncated HMAC, or encrypted and authenticated with AES-256-GCM, and numbered so that a replayed message is refused. Messages longer than an ASDU are cut into segments.

An [Endpoint](#type-endpoint) is one station's end of such an association. It does no I/O: the caller hands it what was received and sends what it returns, which is what the client and server packages do when they are given one (client.WithSecurity, server.WithSecurity). On its own it is useful to test and to analyse.

#### Provenance {#hdr-Provenance}

The normative documents are not public. The message formats, MAC inputs, key derivation and state machines of this package were derived from the open-source implementation github.com/cB-Sigma/iec60870 (Apache-2.0), which states that it follows licensed copies of both standards; the code is this module's own. Interoperability with that implementation is tested (the module interop/cbsigma of this repository); conformance to the standards is not established independently. See SECURITY.md.

## Variables

```go
var (
	HMACSHA256Serial = MACAlgorithm{"HMAC-SHA-256/8", 3, sha256.New, 8}
	HMACSHA256       = MACAlgorithm{"HMAC-SHA-256/16", 4, sha256.New, 16}
)
```

The MAC algorithms. HMAC-SHA-256 is mandatory: truncated to 16 octets on TCP/IP, which is the default here, and to 8 on serial links. HMAC-SHA3-256 (codes 7 and 8) is optional. BLAKE2s (codes 9 and 10) is not implemented.

```go

	HMACSHA3_256Serial = MACAlgorithm{"HMAC-SHA3-256/8", 7, newSHA3, 8}
	HMACSHA3_256       = MACAlgorithm{"HMAC-SHA3-256/16", 8, newSHA3, 16}
)
```

HMAC-SHA3-256, optional in IEC 62351-5.

```go
var (
	// ErrMessage reports a security message that cannot be encoded or
	// decoded: a field out of range, a wrong length, a type or cause that
	// is not permitted in the direction it travels.
	ErrMessage = errors.New("sec: malformed security message")

	// ErrNotReady reports application data that cannot be protected yet:
	// no session keys are established, or the controlling station holds
	// its data back while it changes them. The caller waits for
	// [Endpoint.Changed] and tries again.
	ErrNotReady = errors.New("sec: no secure session")

	// ErrUnsecured reports an ordinary ASDU received on a connection the
	// A-Profile applies to. It is discarded.
	ErrUnsecured = errors.New("sec: unprotected ASDU refused")

	// ErrAuthentication reports a message whose MAC or AEAD tag does not
	// verify, or whose wrapped keys do not unwrap. It is discarded.
	ErrAuthentication = errors.New("sec: authentication failed")

	// ErrReplay reports Secure Data whose sequence number is not above the
	// last one accepted. It is discarded.
	ErrReplay = errors.New("sec: replayed secure data")

	// ErrUnexpected reports a security message that the state machine does
	// not expect now, or whose association IDs do not match. It is
	// discarded.
	ErrUnexpected = errors.New("sec: unexpected security message")

	// ErrCertificate reports a remote certificate that is not valid (wrong
	// curve, outside its validity period, bad signature) or not authorized
	// by [Trust], or a local one that cannot be used.
	ErrCertificate = errors.New("sec: certificate refused")

	// ErrAlgorithm reports an algorithm the remote station selected that
	// this station does not support or does not accept.
	ErrAlgorithm = errors.New("sec: algorithm not supported")

	// ErrProcedure reports that a Station Association or Session Key Change
	// failed: the remote station did not answer within the expected reply
	// time, repeatedly.
	ErrProcedure = errors.New("sec: key management procedure failed")

	// ErrConfig reports a [Config] an Endpoint cannot run with.
	ErrConfig = errors.New("sec: invalid configuration")
)
```

Errors of the package. They are usually wrapped with detail; test with errors.Is.

## Functions

### func AssociationOf

```go
func AssociationOf(raw []byte, p asdu.Params) (aim uint16, ok bool)
```

AssociationOf returns the AIM, the controlling station's half of the association ID, of a received wire ASDU: every security message carries it first, so the first segment of one names the association it belongs to. ok is false for anything else, a later segment included. A controlled station that serves several controlling stations uses it to pick the Endpoint for a connection.

### func Authorized

```go
func Authorized(roles []AccessRole, t asdu.TypeID) bool
```

Authorized reports whether any of the roles may request type t.

### func Decode

```go
func Decode(b []byte, p asdu.Params, d Direction) (Header, Message, error)
```

Decode parses a whole security ASDU (no segmentation control octet) that travels in direction d. The type must be a security type with the cause of transmission permitted for it in that direction. A MAC is returned as the trailing octets; its length is checked when it is verified.

### func Encode

```go
func Encode(h Header, p asdu.Params, m Message) ([]byte, error)
```

Encode returns the whole security ASDU: h, whose Type is taken from m, and the fields of m. It has no segmentation control octet; see [Segment](#func-segment).

### func PermittedCause

```go
func PermittedCause(t asdu.TypeID, d Direction) (asdu.Cause, bool)
```

PermittedCause returns the cause of transmission a security message of type t carries in direction d, and false when t is not a security type or does not travel in that direction.

### func Segment

```go
func Segment(msg []byte, p asdu.Params, max int, seq uint8) ([][]byte, uint8, error)
```

Segment cuts a whole security message into wire ASDUs of at most max octets: each the data unit identifier, an ASC octet and the next part of the fields. seq numbers the first segment; the number after the last one is returned. A message that fits is one segment with FIR and FIN set.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Role of the station: Controlling (the client) or Controlled (the
	// server).
	Role Role

	// AssociationID is this station's half of the association ID, 1 to
	// 65535: the AIM of a controlling station, the AIS of a controlled one.
	AssociationID uint16

	// Identity is the station's certificate and private key, needed for
	// the Station Association. Without it only an association kept in
	// Store can be used.
	Identity *Identity

	// Trust says which remote stations may associate.
	Trust Trust

	// IgnoreValidity accepts certificates outside their validity period,
	// for devices without a reliable clock.
	IgnoreValidity bool

	// MAC is the MAC algorithm a controlling station selects for the key
	// management messages and the key derivation; default
	// [HMACSHA256].Code.
	MAC uint8

	// DataProtection is the algorithm a controlling station selects for
	// Secure Data: a MAC algorithm code or [AES256GCM]; default MAC.
	DataProtection uint8

	// AcceptMAC and AcceptDataProtection limit what a controlled station
	// accepts. Empty accepts every algorithm this package implements.
	AcceptMAC            []uint8
	AcceptDataProtection []uint8

	// Settings are the timers and key usage limits.
	Settings Settings

	// Store keeps the association over reconnects and restarts. Nil keeps
	// it in a MemoryStore of the Endpoint.
	Store KeyStore

	// Params are the ASDU field sizes; zero means asdu.IEC104.
	Params asdu.Params

	// CommonAddr and Originator fill the data unit identifier of the key
	// management messages this station sends.
	CommonAddr asdu.CommonAddr
	Originator uint8

	// Roles are the roles of the controlling station at a controlled
	// station, for [Endpoint.Permits]. Nil applies no role-based access
	// control: every request is permitted.
	Roles []AccessRole

	// OnEvent is called for every security event (a statistic with an
	// event mnemonic was incremented). It is called without locks held,
	// on the goroutine that drove the Endpoint, and must not block.
	OnEvent func(Event)

	// Rand is the source of random data and keys; nil uses crypto/rand.
	Rand io.Reader
}
```

Config configures one end of an association.

### type Curve

```go
type Curve uint8
```

Curve is the elliptic curve of a station's key pair. Both stations of an association use the same curve: the Station Association is an ECDH key agreement between the keys of their certificates.

IEC 62351-5 also lists secp256k1, Curve448 and brainpoolP256r1. The Go standard library has none of them, and this module depends on nothing else, so they are not supported.

```go
const (
	// P256 is secp256r1 (NIST P-256). A P-256 key can sign, so a station
	// with one can have a self-signed certificate.
	P256 Curve = iota + 1
	// X25519 is Curve25519. It serves key agreement only: the certificate
	// must be signed by a Central Authority.
	X25519
)
```

### type Endpoint

```go
type Endpoint struct {

	// ASC sequence number of the next segment sent

	// the latest time the caller passed

	// the association

	// valid update keys

	// controlling station

	// reply timeouts in the running procedure
	// whole request last sent, for retransmission and MACs

	// the Session Request sent

	// the Session Initiation Request received (controlling) or sent (controlled)

	// controlled station

	// no Session Initiation Request before this

	// the session

	// controlled: the session keys are of an earlier connection

}
```

Endpoint is one station's end of an association: the Station Association, Session Key Change and Secure Data state machines of either role.

It does no I/O and keeps no time of its own. The caller reports the connection with [Endpoint.Up](#func-endpoint-up) and [Endpoint.Down](#func-endpoint-down), passes every received ASDU to [Endpoint.Receive](#func-endpoint-receive), every application ASDU to send to [Endpoint.Protect](#func-endpoint-protect), and calls [Endpoint.Tick](#func-endpoint-tick) at [Endpoint.Deadline](#func-endpoint-deadline). Each returns the wire ASDUs to send, in order, on the connection that carries the association.

The connections of a redundancy group share one association: the one with data transfer started carries it. [Endpoint.Attach](#func-endpoint-attach) and [Endpoint.Detach](#func-endpoint-detach) do the bookkeeping for callers that run several.

An Endpoint is safe for concurrent use.

#### func New

```go
func New(cfg Config) (*Endpoint, error)
```

New returns an Endpoint for cfg. It loads the association kept in cfg.Store: update keys stay valid, session keys do not.

#### func (Endpoint) Attach

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Attach(owner any, now time.Time) [][]byte
```

Attach reports that data transfer started on the connection owner; it carries the association from now on. A connection that carried it before is detached first. It returns what to send.

#### func (Endpoint) Changed

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Changed() <-chan struct{}
```

Changed returns a channel that is closed at the next change of the association that callers may wait for: session keys became valid or invalid, a procedure failed, or work is due ([Endpoint.Reassociate](#func-endpoint-reassociate), [Endpoint.Renew](#func-endpoint-renew)).

#### func (Endpoint) Deadline

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Deadline() time.Time
```

Deadline returns when [Endpoint.Tick](#func-endpoint-tick) must be called next; the zero time when no timer runs. A time not after the latest time passed in means at once.

#### func (Endpoint) Detach

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Detach(owner any)
```

Detach reports that data transfer stopped or the connection owner ended. It is ignored when owner does not carry the association.

#### func (Endpoint) Down

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Down()
```

Down reports that the connection was lost or data transfer stopped. A running procedure fails. The keys stay: the next connection uses them.

#### func (Endpoint) Err

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Err() error
```

Err returns why the last key management procedure failed, or nil.

#### func (Endpoint) Owns

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Owns(owner any) bool
```

Owns reports whether owner carries the association.

#### func (Endpoint) Permits

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Permits(t asdu.TypeID) bool
```

Permits reports whether the roles of the controlling station allow a request of type t (see [Config.Roles](#func-config-roles)). The controlled station answers a refused request with a negative confirmation with cause [asdu.CauseNotAuthorized](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#CauseNotAuthorized); call [Endpoint.Refused](#func-endpoint-refused) to count it.

#### func (Endpoint) Protect

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Protect(now time.Time, data []byte) ([][]byte, error)
```

Protect wraps an application ASDU in Secure Data and returns its segments. It returns ErrNotReady while no session keys may be used; the caller waits for [Endpoint.Changed](#func-endpoint-changed). The segments must be sent in order and before anything else this Endpoint returns later: the receiver accepts only increasing sequence numbers.

#### func (Endpoint) Ready

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Ready() bool
```

Ready reports whether application data can be protected now.

#### func (Endpoint) Reassociate

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Reassociate() error
```

Reassociate asks a controlling station to run the Station Association again, at the next Tick when no procedure is running.

#### func (Endpoint) Receive

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Receive(now time.Time, raw []byte) (data []byte, out [][]byte, err error)
```

Receive takes one ASDU received on the connection that carries the association. It returns the application ASDU it carried, if any, and what to send. An error says why a message was discarded; the association goes on.

Refused counts a request refused by role-based access control.

#### func (Endpoint) Up

```go
func (e *Endpoint) Up(now time.Time) [][]byte
```

Up reports that the connection is established with data transfer started. Every connection begins with fresh session keys. A controlling station starts the key management: the Station Association when it has no update keys, otherwise a Session Key Change. A controlled station holds what it sends until new session keys arrive, accepts data under the previous ones meanwhile, and asks for new ones with a Session Initiation Request unless the controlling station changes them first. It returns what to send.

### type Permission

```go
type Permission uint8
```

Permission is one of the permissions of IEC TS 60870-5-7 role-based access control.

```go
const (
	PermMonitorData Permission = 1 << iota
	PermOperateControls
	PermFileRead
	PermFileWrite
	PermFileManagement
	PermConfigOperation
	PermConfigSecurity
)
```

The permissions.

#### func RequiredPermission

```go
func RequiredPermission(t asdu.TypeID) Permission
```

RequiredPermission is the permission a request of type t needs. The standard leaves the mapping to the implementation; this one follows github.com/cB-Sigma/iec60870: commands and set points need operate controls; interrogation and read need monitor data; parameters and the reset process need config operation; the file service needs file read (call, directory, log query, and the acknowledgement of what was read) or file write. Clock synchronization, test and everything else need nothing.

F\_AF\_NA\_1 needs file read: from a controlling station it can only acknowledge a section or file it downloaded, since in an upload the controlled station acknowledges. cB-Sigma/iec60870 v0.3.0 asks for file write, which lets a viewer read a whole file and then refuses its acknowledgement.

### type Settings

```go
type Settings struct {
	// ReplyTimeout is how long a controlling station waits for each answer
	// of the remote station before it sends the request again. Default 2 s.
	ReplyTimeout time.Duration

	// MaxReplyTimeouts is how many times in a row a controlling station
	// waits in vain before the procedure fails. Default 3.
	MaxReplyTimeouts int

	// RequestTimeout is how long a controlled station waits for the next
	// request of a procedure it answered. Default 6 s.
	RequestTimeout time.Duration

	// KeyLifetime and KeyUses limit how long and for how many messages a
	// pair of session keys is used: a controlling station changes them when
	// either is reached, a controlled station stops accepting them.
	// Defaults 15 minutes and 1000 messages at a controlling station,
	// twice that at a controlled one, which must allow more than its peer.
	KeyLifetime time.Duration
	KeyUses     uint32
}
```

Settings are the timers and key usage limits of an association. A zero field takes its default.

### type Stat

```go
type Stat uint8
```

Stat is one of the security statistics of IEC TS 60870-5-7 (the counters of IEC 62351-5), in the order of its table.

```go
const (
	StatSuccessfulAssociations Stat = iota
	StatAssociationFailures
	StatSuccessfulSessionKeyChanges
	StatSessionKeyChangeFailures
	StatKeyInvalidationsTime
	StatKeyInvalidationsCount
	StatProtocolInformationErrors
	StatKeyAuthAlgorithmFailures
	StatKeyWrapAlgorithmFailures
	StatDataProtectionAlgorithmFailures
	StatKeyAuthenticationErrors
	StatDataAuthenticationErrors
	StatUnexpectedMessages
	StatMaxReplyTimeouts
	StatRemoteAuthorizationFailures
	StatOperationAuthorizationFailures
	StatRemoteCertificateFailures
	StatRemoteCertificateExpirations
	StatRemoteCertificateRevocations
	StatLocalCertificateExpirations
	StatLocalCertificateRevocations
	StatKeyInvalidationsRemoteRevocation
	StatKeyInvalidationsLocalRevocation
	StatSuccessfulDataAuthentications
	StatReplyTimeouts
	StatRequestTimeouts
	StatMessagesSent
	StatMessagesReceived
	StatDiscardedMessages
	NumStats
)
```

The statistics.

#### func (Stat) Event

```go
func (s Stat) Event() (string, Severity, bool)
```

Event returns the mnemonic and severity of the security event of IEC 62351-5 that the statistic announces, and false when it has none.

#### func (Stat) String

```go
func (s Stat) String() string
```

String is the statistic's name.

### type State

```go
type State struct {
	AIM               uint16 `json:"aim"`
	AIS               uint16 `json:"ais"`
	MAC               uint8  `json:"mal"`
	KeyWrap           uint8  `json:"kwa"`
	EncryptionKey     []byte `json:"encryptionUpdateKey,omitempty"`
	AuthenticationKey []byte `json:"authenticationUpdateKey,omitempty"`
	RemoteCertificate []byte `json:"remoteCertificate,omitempty"`
	ControlKey        []byte `json:"controlSessionKey,omitempty"`
	MonitorKey        []byte `json:"monitorSessionKey,omitempty"`
	DataProtection    uint8  `json:"dpa,omitempty"`
}
```

State is what one end of an association keeps over a restart: the association IDs and algorithms, the update keys, the remote certificate and the last session keys. Everything but the IDs and the certificate is secret: a [KeyStore](#type-keystore) must protect it and must never log it.

The session keys are kept only so that a controlled station can authenticate the Session Initiation Request that asks for new ones; they are not used for data after a restart.

### type Statistics

```go
type Statistics [NumStats]uint32
```

Statistics are the counters of one association. The counters wrap after 2^32-1.

### type Status

```go
type Status struct {
	Role Role
	// Up reports whether a connection with data transfer started carries
	// the association.
	Up bool
	// Associated reports valid update keys; Ready valid session keys that
	// may be used now.
	Associated, Ready bool
	// State names the state of the key management.
	State    string
	AIM, AIS uint16
	MAC      string // the MAC algorithm of the association
	Data     string // the data protection algorithm of the session
	// Remote is the remote station's certificate, nil before an
	// association.
	Remote *x509.Certificate
	// Err is why the last key management procedure failed, nil after a
	// success.
	Err error
}
```

Status describes an association. It holds no keys.

### type Trust

```go
type Trust struct {
	// Fingerprints are SHA-256 digests of accepted self-signed
	// certificates (see [Fingerprint]).
	Fingerprints [][32]byte
	// PublicKeys are accepted self-signed certificates' public keys, as
	// carried in the certificate (the subjectPublicKey bit string).
	PublicKeys [][]byte
	// Authorities are the Central Authority certificates that may sign
	// remote station certificates.
	Authorities []*x509.Certificate
	// Subjects, when not empty, restricts the stations a Central Authority
	// vouches for to these subject names (DER, as in
	// x509.Certificate.RawSubject).
	Subjects [][]byte
}
```

Trust is what a station accepts as the other end of an association.

A self-signed remote certificate is accepted when its fingerprint or its public key is listed. A certificate signed by one of the Central Authorities is accepted when Subjects is empty or lists its subject.
